Errors are thrown and produce a failure exit code, which is handled.
Its output must be inspected by a person before any result is accepted.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Options, output folder and sparse project lookup
sections.what: Reads the command options, prepares the output folder, and finds the one dairy project with the fewest active quotes. That project becomes the sparse test group.
sections.why: Likely reason: it selects a thin-evidence case automatically so the test covers a low-data situation.
sections.watch_out: The output folder is resolved from the current working directory, so running from another folder writes files somewhere unexpected.

sections.name: cohorts
sections.title: Test groups
sections.what: Defines the two groups: a fixed rich nuclear pair of projects and the sparse dairy project. When expanded mode is on, only the nuclear group is kept.
sections.why: The code comment says the user approved the extra pass only for the two nuclear projects.
sections.watch_out: The nuclear project IDs are hardcoded, so they must be updated by hand if the data changes.

sections.name: report (part 1)
sections.title: Freezing inputs and starting runs
sections.what: For each group, confirms the scope matches its frozen IDs, saves a snapshot of the inputs, and creates a new run or reuses one. In continuation mode it copies earlier gathered facts into a new run and sets the run to reuse captured sources.
sections.why: Likely reason: a frozen snapshot makes the test repeatable, and continuation lets an interrupted run carry on without fetching everything again.
sections.watch_out: Continuation assumes the parent run has a gather stage. If it does not, the script throws and stops.

sections.name: report: if
sections.title: Waiting for runs to finish
sections.what: Starts each run, checks its status every two seconds, and logs stage changes. When the run reaches a final state, saves its stage records and report. If 25 minutes pass, marks the run cancelled and stops.
sections.why: Gives each group a clear final result and keeps the script from waiting forever.
sections.watch_out: On timeout the message says the checkpoint is kept, but the stored data is not verified here, so check it before relying on a resume.

summary: Live test script that starts two limited research runs on fixed groups of projects and records whether they finished.
purpose: Checks that the native Lessons Learnt research pipeline completes on a rich nuclear group and a sparse dairy group, and saves reports in docs/verification.
why: The header says it is a bounded live acceptance check. Freezing the scope keeps the test repeatable. Reason for the expanded mode is in the code comment: the user approved an extra pass for the two nuclear projects only.
how: Reads command options: expanded, resume, continue-from, capture-only and review-only. Finds one dairy project with the fewest active quotes. Builds two groups. For each group, checks that the scope resolves to the exact frozen IDs, saves a frozen snapshot of the inputs, creates or reuses a run record, and in continuation mode copies the earlier gathered facts. Starts the run and checks its status every two seconds for up to 25 minutes. Saves stage records and a status report, then exits with success only if every group succeeded.
inputs: Command options; the projects, evidence_quotes and Lessons Learnt tables; an earlier native-live-acceptance.json when resuming; primary-source-candidates.json when continuing.
outputs: Frozen input files, native-live-acceptance.json, stage record files in docs/verification, and new run rows in the database.
risks: Creates real Lessons Learnt run records. Continuation copies stored facts from a parent run. On timeout it marks the run cancelled. A run that completes is reported as pending inspection, not as accepted.
debug: Open native-live-acceptance.json to see each group's status, error and prior attempts. Open the frozen input files to see what was tested. If resume fails, confirm the prior report file exists in the expected folder.
